Then the years and days on which some adversity befell the body of such a person must be carefully explored; these being perceived, I inquire in the ephemerides whether on such a day, when that adversity happened, one of the malefics, such as Saturn or Mars, strikes the degree of the ascendant of the erected figure, either by bodily transit or by a bad ray. If these things have happened in this way, I say that the degree of such a malefic is the true ascendant of the nativity. Saturn, indeed, by bodily transit, or by its opposing square, causes, according to its nature, melancholic passions both of body and of mind; Mars, passing over the ascendant of the birth, stirs up anger, wounds, and Martial infirmities. The lord of the ascendant, moreover, is to be examined when it is carried through the places of the unfortunate stars, or when it meets evil and unlucky rays. But since certain bodily accidents happen not through transits over the ascendant but through profections, or through the directions of the significators to the promissors, another way must be taken. In those things which happen through annual profections, one must look carefully whether the annual profection of the ascendant of the proposed nativity can reach the body or the malignant rays of some malefic; and if this has happened, the intervening days between the day of birth and the day of the accident are to be counted; these days are then to be extended by six, that is, multiplied by six, and they become sixths of days. I divide these sixths of days by 73 (for 73 sixths of days make one degree in annual profections), and the resulting number shows the degrees and the remaining minutes. I subtract these degrees and minutes from the place of the promissor or significator of the accident, and what remains will be the true degree and minute of the ascendant of the proposed nativity. For example, let someone be born in the year 1477, on 16 January, at the eleventh hour after noon, in latitude 50 degrees. Then, in the year completed at 58, on 1 January, he fell from a height, almost fatally, and the cause of the fall was Saturn retrograde in Leo and in the tenth house. Through this notable accident, which thus proceeded from the root of the nativity, the degree of the ascendant of the proposed nativity is to be examined. Now the annual profection of the ascendant is found to have fallen in that year to Cancer, and before the year was completed the aforesaid profection reaches the sign of Leo, in which Saturn was in the root of the nativity. Now therefore the days must be counted, first the intervening days from the day of birth to the first of January, the year of the accident, and they are found to be 349, which, increased by six, make 2094 sixths of days. These, divided by 73 sixths, yield 28 degrees 50 minutes, which are to be subtracted from the place of the promissor of the accident, namely from 4 signs 20 degrees 32 minutes, the place of Saturn; and there will remain 21 degrees 42 minutes, the true degree of the ascendant, namely of the sign of Libra. For the rectification or verification of the proposed nativity through the direction of the ascendant to the malefics or their malignant rays, one proceeds thus: first the oblique ascension of the promissor of the accident for the latitude of the region must be sought, and from it the degrees and minutes due to the completed years from the birth, up to the year and day of the accident, are to be subtracted (for each year is worth one degree and each six days one minute in directions); and what remains will be the oblique ascension of the true ascendant. Seek this oblique ascension in the table of oblique ascensions for the same region, and you will find the true degree of the ascendant of the aforesaid nativity. So, in the fortieth completed year of life, the man whose nativity I have now proposed to rectify was much infected with scabies, with ulcers and apostemes, and other melancholic affections, which was a notable accident of the significators of Saturn. About the same time he also experienced febrile passions. When the direction was examined, the degree of the ascendant of this man's nativity, applied to the malefics of the accidents of that same year, was found to have applied, around those days, the direction of the ascendant to the square of Saturn, which was at 20 degrees 32 minutes of Scorpio. The oblique ascension of this is 250 degrees 46 minutes. From this, on account of the 40 years and 192 days, 40 degrees 32 minutes are to be subtracted, and there will remain 210 degrees 14 minutes, namely the oblique ascension of the true ascendant, which showed 21 degrees and almost 40 minutes of Libra, the true ascendant of the nativity. In the same way one must proceed also with the other promissors and significators, and the kinds of the various accidents and events must be noted with care, from the progressions or directions to the principal places in the theme or figure, such as the ascendant, the midheaven, and also the Sun and Moon. For when Saturn, or its square or opposition, meets the ascendant through progression, that meeting portends to the one born cold and dry diseases and melancholic disturbances. And this meeting is almost always fatal to old men. Moreover, it hinders all success in counsels, and burdens the one born with heavier cares, and as it were oppresses him with pains of mind. But this must be carefully noted: if Saturn, or its unlucky rays, meet the ascendant or the Moon in fiery signs, such as Leo, Sagittarius and Aries, it then threatens a dyscrasia and a conflict of cold and hot, which will assail the body. But if it meets in earthy signs, such as Taurus, Virgo or Capricorn, it threatens vicious and melancholic apostemes; in airy signs, such as Gemini, Libra and Aquarius, it stirs up winds harmful to the body and sometimes poisonous; in watery signs, finally, such as Cancer, Pisces and Scorpio, it produces phlegmatic vices. Sometimes it disfigures the body of the one born with scars and other defects, by which a limb loses its function, as in contractions; and it does this in those parts of the body which the nature of that sign governs, in which the unlucky meeting occurs.

units.la: Ascendenti vero occurrens Jupiter, ejus sextilis, trigo-nusve, nato promittit prosperam corporis valetudinem, felicesq; successus ac conversationes cum Jovialibus, ut Episcopis, Prælatis, Jureconsultis, & præstantioribus viris equestris ordinis, & præterea aliquod etiam commodum emolumentumq; accedet ad natum, sive eum, cujus genitura fuerit, ex natura & proprietate signi & domus, in qua occursus ille contingit.
units.tr: When Jupiter meets the Ascendant by sextile or trine, it promises the native good bodily health, happy success, and dealings with men of Jupiter's kind, such as bishops, prelates, jurists, and the more distinguished men of the equestrian order. Some benefit and profit will also come to the native, whoever the one whose nativity it is, according to the nature and character of the sign and the house in which this meeting occurs.

units.la: Ascendenti occursans Mars, ejus quadratus vel oppositus, natum inquietabit calidis ęgritudinibus, febribus malignis, iracundia, rixis, vulneribus, infelicibus itineribus, læsione ab igne, casu ab alto, dysenteria, cholerae incendio, tuncq; nati actiones ob contentiones & similia retardabuntur.
units.tr: When Mars meets the Ascendant by square or opposition, it will trouble the native with hot diseases, malignant fevers, anger, quarrels, wounds, unlucky journeys, injury from fire, a fall from a height, dysentery, and bile-fired inflammations, and the native's undertakings will then be delayed by disputes and the like.

units.la: Trinus vero vel sextilis Martis occurrens Ascendenti, reddit audaciam, in contentionibusq; & pugnis victoriam, erigitq; nati animum ad bellicas artes exercendas, ad hastiludia tractan-da, & hostem adoriendum, & tunc temporis non infeliciter tra-ctabit bellica tormenta, & quicquid arte quadam per ignes & fusiones metallicas tentabit, succedet.
units.tr: But when Mars meets the Ascendant by trine or sextile, it gives boldness, victory in contests and fights, and stirs the native's spirit to take up the military arts, to handle jousting, and to attack an enemy. At that time the native will handle siege engines without misfortune, and whatever he attempts by some art involving fire and the casting of metals will succeed.

units.la: Inprimis vero advertendum, cùm Saturnus vel Mars A-scendenti occurrit in signis sanguineis, ut geminis, libra, vel A-quario, sanguinem tunc perturbari, agitariq;, mentisq; securitatem atq; hilaritatem obtundi. In signis cholericis, ut leone, sagittario, & ariete, ad iracundiam, audaciam, & temeritatem in-rebus agendis, consiliisq; capessendis natum excitari, disponiq; ad ægritudines calidas: in melancholicis, ut tauro, virgine, & capricorno, melancholicas augeri curas & cogitationes: in-phlegmaticis, ut cancro, scorpione, & piscibus, somnolentos, inertes, & ad negotia subeunda inidoneos reddi.
units.tr: Above all it must be noted that when Saturn or Mars meets the Ascendant in the sanguine signs, such as Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius, the blood is then disturbed and stirred, and the mind's calm and cheerfulness are blunted. In the choleric signs, such as Leo, Sagittarius, and Aries, the native is roused to anger, boldness, and rashness in carrying out affairs and taking up plans, and is disposed to hot diseases. In the melancholic signs, such as Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, the native's melancholy cares and thoughts are increased. In the phlegmatic signs, such as Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, he is made drowsy, sluggish, and unfit to undertake business.

units.la: Sed Mercurii quadratus vel oppositus ad ascendens per progressionem perveniens, nō parum infortunii & contentionis denotabit, præsertim in contractibus, aliisque actionibus Mercurialibus. Reddet quoque hic occursus hebetiores & ob-tusiores, ingeniiq; culturam non admittit: in infantia, si contigerit, variolis corpus infestat[?] cum læsione dentium, linguæ & gutturis.
units.tr: But when Mercury comes to the Ascendant by square or opposition, arriving by progression, it will signify no small misfortune and strife, especially in contracts and other Mercurial activities. This meeting also makes a person duller and more obtuse, and does not admit the cultivation of the mind. In infancy, if it happens, it afflicts the body with smallpox, with injury to the teeth, tongue, and throat.

units.la: Cauda draconis, seu nodus descendens occurrens horo-scopo, vitæ discrimen significat, corpusq; de natura Martis & Saturni morbis impugnat, visumq; debilitat, ac inimicorum potestatem & vexationem importat.
units.tr: The Dragon's Tail, or the descending node, meeting the horoscope, signifies danger to life. It attacks the body with diseases of the nature of Mars and Saturn, weakens the sight, and brings the power and harassment of enemies.

units.la: Lunæ progressiones, eos præmonstrant eventus, quę contingunt circa mores, animi affectiones, & conversationes hu-manas, graves, prudentes, placidas, honestas, mites, magnani-mas: aut contrà, leves, inconstantes, insipientes, dissolutas, tru-culentas, suspicaces: item hilares, amicabiles: aut contra, tristes, tetricasq;, & immundas.
units.tr: The progressions of the Moon show the events that come about in respect of manners, states of mind, and human dealings: serious, prudent, calm, honest, gentle, magnanimous; or on the contrary, frivolous, inconstant, foolish, dissolute, savage, suspicious; likewise cheerful and friendly; or on the contrary, sad, gloomy, and filthy.

units.la: Lunæ igitur occurrens Saturnus, ejus quadratus vel oppositus, movet natum ad tristes & melancholicas cogitationes, quibus agitatus facilè ob humorum abundantiam in febres incurret, implicatq; hic occursus natum multis curis & sollicitudinibus, animiq; anxietatem inducit cum corporis languore, quem alia valetudinis incommoda comitantur. Si verò sextili vel trigono Lunam pulsaverit, omnia prosperiora erunt.
units.tr: When Saturn meets the Moon, by square or opposition, it moves the native to sad and melancholy thoughts. Stirred by these, he easily falls into fevers because of an abundance of humours. This meeting also entangles the native in many cares and anxieties and brings anxiety of mind together with bodily weakness, which is accompanied by other ailments of health. But if Saturn strikes the Moon by sextile or trine, all will be more favourable.

units.la: Lunæ occurrens Mars, ejus quadratus aut oppositus, dissidia & contentiones suscitabit periculosas, oculorumq; dolores acutos.
units.tr: When Mars meets the Moon, by square or opposition, it will stir up dangerous quarrels and disputes, and sharp pains in the eyes.

units.la: Lunæ occurrens cauda draconis, præterquam quòd nocet visui, natum conjicit in vehementes animi motus, iram & contentiones, veneniq; & ventris profluvii per cibum vel potum metum & suspicionem.
units.tr: When the Dragon's Tail meets the Moon, besides harming the sight, it throws the native into violent emotions, anger and disputes, and fear and suspicion of poison or of a flux of the bowels through food or drink.

units.la: Lunæ verò occurrens Mercurius, ejus sextilis vel trigonus, nato significabit incommoda à Mercurialibus, eruditorum odium & invidiam, altercationesq; noxias cum iisdem, per dolum aut criminis alicujus falsi commissum, in literis, rationibus vel contractibus: hic etiam occursus facit, ut natus male audiat præter suam culpam, reddit enim eum exosum apud vulgus.
units.tr: But when Mercury meets the Moon by sextile or trine, it signifies to the native troubles from Mercurial people, the hatred and envy of learned men, and harmful quarrels with them, through deceit or the committing of some false charge, in writings, accounts, or contracts. This meeting also causes the native to be ill spoken of through no fault of his own, for it makes him hateful to the common people.

units.la: Medii Cœli progressiones observantur ad prævidendos eventus de magistratibus & honoribus, quos subditi in natum collaturi sunt: præmonstrant, inquam, ad quæ Reipublicæ munia subditi vocaturi sint natum, quæ nati sit futura autoritas, eminentia aut amplitudo in Magistratu, & ad quos honores, artisq; genus natus sit aspiraturus.
units.tr: The progressions of the Midheaven are observed in order to foresee events concerning magistrates and honours that subjects are going to confer on the native. They show, I say, to which duties of the commonwealth subjects are going to summon the native, what authority, eminence, or amplitude in office he is going to have, and to which honours and kind of art he will aspire.

units.la: Quando igitur Medio Cœli, aut ejus Domino occurrit Saturnus, vel suo corpore, vel quadrato aut trigono, judicandum est, subditos adversaturos, imò insidiaturos dignitatibus & honoribus ejus, cujus est genitura: & circa id tempus studia, artes, actiones & negotia infeliciter cedent, & ita retardabuntur, ut non nisi cum damno perficiantur.
units.tr: When Saturn meets the Midheaven, or its lord, either in its own body or by square or trine, it is to be judged that subjects will oppose, indeed plot against, the dignities and honours of the one whose nativity it is. About that time studies, arts, actions, and affairs will turn out unhappily, and will be delayed so that they are completed only with loss.

units.la: Sed Medio Cœli occurrens Jovis fulgor, nato confert honores, dignitates, amicitiam Jovialem, gratiam, inq; actionibus & studiis felicem & prosperum successum.
units.tr: But the splendour of Jupiter meeting the Midheaven confers honours, dignities, Jovial friendship, and favour on the native, and a happy and prosperous outcome in his undertakings and studies.

units.la: Medio vero cœli occurrens Martis horrendus rubor, reddit nato infensos homines Martiales, qui se opponent honoribus & dignitatibus nati: quare prudenter sibi cavebit, ne ab illis injuriis & calumniis impetitus, dignitatis & honoris patiatur jacturam.
units.tr: But the dreadful redness of Mars meeting the Midheaven makes men of Martial character hostile to the native, and they will oppose the native's honours and dignities. Therefore he will prudently guard himself, lest, assailed by their injuries and calumnies, he suffer the loss of his dignity and honour.

units.la: Mercurii Medio cœli quadratus vel oppositus radius occurrens, honores, dignitatem, officia, omnesq; actiones nati, insidiis, dolis, mendaciis, variisq; technis impugnabit.
units.tr: A ray of Mercury meeting the Midheaven by square or opposition will attack the native's honours, dignity, offices, and all his actions with plots, deceits, lies, and various tricks.

units.la: Cauda draconis Medio cœli occurrens, dignitates & honores nati macula aliqua aspergit, actionesq; & negotia multa interrumpit, quæ bonum aliás sortita fuissent effectum.
units.tr: The Dragon's Tail meeting the Midheaven stains the native's dignities and honours with some blemish, and interrupts many actions and affairs that would otherwise have had a good outcome.

units.la: Solis denique progressiones observantur ad providendos eventus de honoribus & dignitate, qui nato conferuntur a Regibus, Principibus, aut aliis, in eximia quadam seu præeminente dignitate constitutis. Quin per Solis progressiones erudite licet æstimare, æquóne & benevolo, an vero iniquo animo Principes, & qui rerum gubernaculis præsident, affecti sint erga natum.
units.tr: Finally, the progressions of the Sun are observed in order to foresee events concerning honours and dignity conferred on the native by kings, princes, or others placed in some outstanding or pre-eminent rank. Indeed, through the progressions of the Sun a learned person may judge whether the princes and those who preside over the helm of affairs are disposed towards the native with a fair and kindly mind, or with an unfair one.

units.la: Cùm enim Soli occurrit Saturnus, ejus quadratus aut oppositus, natus experietur Principes, Magistratusq;, alieno semper erga se esse animo: trinus vero vel sextilis ejusdem radius, honores confert, & dignitates, quas habet, nato conservat.
units.tr: For when Saturn meets the Sun, by square or opposition, the native will always experience princes and magistrates disposed towards him with an unfriendly mind. But a ray of the same by trine or sextile confers honours and dignities, and preserves for the native those which he has.

units.la: Jupiter vel ipse, vel sextili, aut trigono Soli obvians, nato pollicetur, honores, dignitates, & publicam quandam præeminentiam aut officium, indecq; claram famam.
units.tr: Jupiter, either itself or by sextile or trine, meeting the Sun, promises the native honours, dignities, a certain public pre-eminence or office, and a clear reputation.

units.la: Sed Soli occurrens Mars, Principum, aut eorum, qui Principum gerunt vices, animos à nato abalienat, quam postea abalienationem sequuntur alia incommoda, ut publici officii ereptio, aut in exilium ejectio: & haec mala intenduntur, si Mars ita Soli occurset in 12. domo: &, ut dici solet, nullam calamitatem esse solam, ita hic quoq; occursus non solum honores nati impugnat, sed corpus etiam infestat, & humores, aut vitae periculum per casum ex alto portendit.
units.tr: But Mars meeting the Sun alienates the minds of princes, or of those who hold the place of princes, from the native. This alienation is followed by other misfortunes, such as the loss of a public office or expulsion into exile. These evils are intensified if Mars meets the Sun in the twelfth house. And, as is commonly said, one calamity never comes alone; so this meeting not only attacks the native's honours but also afflicts the body, and portends danger from humours, or danger to life through a fall from a height.

units.la: Cauda draconis Soli occursans oculos & visum debilitat, praecipuè vero oculo dextro malum minatur: quin & officiis & honoribus nati adversatur.
units.tr: The Dragon's Tail meeting the Sun weakens the eyes and sight, and threatens harm especially to the right eye. Indeed it is also adverse to the native's offices and honours.

units.la: Si vero Mercurius, sextilis ejus vel quadratus Soli occurrerit, dejicietur natus de officiis Mercurialibus, incidetq; in altercationes & lites, natiq; animum multis & gravibus perturbationibus involvit.
units.tr: If Mercury meets the Sun by sextile or square, the native will be removed from Mercurial offices, will fall into quarrels and lawsuits, and will involve his mind in many grave disturbances.

units.la: Luna deniq; Soli occurrens, nato indicat odium vulgi, hujusq; calumnias, & insuper oculis nocumentum. Haec de progressionibus inferere placuit, ut conspicuum evaderet, non plane vana esse, quae ex iisdem desumuntur, judicia. Nunc reliqua quoq; domicilia cœli persequamur.
units.tr: Finally, the Moon meeting the Sun indicates to the native the hatred of the common people and their slanders, and besides, harm to the eyes. I have thought it fit to set these things out concerning progressions, so that it might become clear that the judgements drawn from them are not altogether vain. Now let us follow the remaining houses of the heavens.

units.la: Horoscopo seu cardini Orientis, seu primae domui succedit infra terrā secunda, suâ natura bona: Septentrionalis, phlegmatica, fœminina: habet collum, guttur, glandulas: dicitur porta inferna, quod ex ea quasi per fores apertas stellae ad horoscopum evehantur. Sumimus ex hac judicium de substantia, divitiis, & facultatibus nati, nec non de modo, quo divitias quis est acquisiturus. In hac Jupiter bene affectus divitiarum affluentiam perpetuam largitur. Consignificator hic est Jupiter ipse.
units.tr: The second house below the earth follows the horoscope, or the cardo of the East, that is, the first house. By its nature it is good; it is northern, phlegmatic, and feminine. It has the neck, throat, and glands. It is called the infernal gate, because the stars are raised to the horoscope through it, as if through open doors. From it we take judgement concerning the substance, riches, and resources of the native, and also concerning the manner in which someone is going to acquire riches. In this house Jupiter, when well disposed, bestows a perpetual abundance of riches. Its co-signifier is Jupiter itself.

units.la: Tertia dicitur cadens, sed à felicium eventuum significatione, Dea: Septentrionalis est, fœminina, phlegmatica: habet humores, brachia, manus. Ex hac judicium colligitur, de fratribus, sororibus, consanguineisq;, nec non itineribus brevibus. Consignificator est Mars, gaudium in ea habet Luna.
units.tr: The third house is called the falling house, but it is a goddess from its signification of fortunate events. It is northern, feminine, and phlegmatic. It has the humours, arms, and hands. From it judgement is drawn concerning brothers, sisters, and blood relations, and also short journeys. Its co-signifier is Mars, and the Moon has its joy in it.

units.la: Quarta sua natura est felix, dicitur angulus terrę, & imum cœli, Septentrionalis est, melancholica, masculina: habet pe-ctus, pulmonem, splenem. Ex hac sumitur judicium de patre, ejusq; statu, de patrimoniis, hæreditatibus, bonis immobilibus, fodinis metallicis, & rebus absconditis. Consignificator est Sol.
units.tr: The fourth house is by its nature fortunate. It is called the angle of the earth and the lower heaven (imum caeli). It is northern, melancholic and masculine, and it governs the chest, lungs and spleen. Judgment is drawn from it concerning the father and his condition, patrimonies, inheritances, immovable goods, metal mines and hidden things. Its co-signifier is the Sun.

units.la: Quinta dicitur bona fortuna, succedens, succedit enim quartæ, & prospera denunciat, est occidentalis, masculina, melancholica: habet stomachum, epar, cor, latera: judicatur ex ea de liberis, delectationibus, gaudio, donationibus, legationibus: hic gaudet Venus, & ipsa est consignificatrix.
units.tr: The fifth house is called good fortune and is succedent, for it follows the fourth and announces prosperity. It is western, masculine and melancholic, and it governs the stomach, liver, heart and sides. Judgment is drawn from it concerning children, pleasures, joy, gifts and embassies. Venus rejoices in this house, and she is its co-signifier.

units.la: Sexta suâ naturâ mala, occidentalis, masculina, melancholica, habet inferiorem ventrem, cum intestinis: significat autem infirmitates & morbos nati, eorumq; quantitate & qualitate, servos; & animalia minora. Consignificator est Mercurius.
units.tr: The sixth house is by its nature evil. It is western, masculine and melancholic, and it governs the lower belly with the intestines. It signifies illnesses and diseases of the native, their extent and kind, servants and smaller animals. Its co-signifier is Mercury.

units.la: Septima, angulus occidentis, masculina, cholerica, occidentalis, habet femora, renes, lumbos, Luna est consignificatrix: judicatur ex hoc cardine de re & statu rei uxoriæ & nuptiarum, contentionibus atque simultatibus, damnisq; ex his resul-tantibus. In hac Mars & Saturnus multis fuerunt funesti, cum-primis vero si Mars hoc in loco fuerit in cancro à Saturno afflictus, cujus rei vel sexcenta liceret proferre exempla. Saturnus vero calamitosus & exitialis hic deprehensus est in signis bestialibus, ut leone, tauro, &c. Si utrq; in hoc angulo tempore ali-cujus nativitatis fuerit constitutus, ita ut in uno signo conjun-gantur, impossibile est, eum violentæ mortis exitum posse evi-tare, nisi per sextilem aut trigonum, Jupiter vel Venus respiciat, vel piis à Deo precibus id impediatur. Genus autem mortis co-gnoscitur ex natura signi, in quo conjunguntur. Si enim conjun-guntur in signis aqueis, mors & periculū denotatur per aquas: in igneis, per ferrum, combustionem & ignem: in terreis, per casum ab alto, ruinam, & id genus alia: in aereis, per strangula-tionem, catharrum suffocativum, decollationem, &c.
units.tr: The seventh house is the angle of the west. It is masculine, choleric and western, and it governs the thighs, kidneys and loins. Its co-signifier is the Moon. Judgment is drawn from this cardo concerning a wife and the state of marriage and weddings, quarrels and enmities, and the losses that result from them. Mars and Saturn have proved baleful to many in this house, above all if Mars is here in Cancer and afflicted by Saturn; one could offer six hundred examples of this. Saturn is found calamitous and deadly here in the beastly signs, such as Leo, Taurus and so on. If both planets are placed in this angle at the time of some birth, so as to be conjoined in one sign, it is impossible for that person to escape a violent death, unless Jupiter or Venus looks on by sextile or trine, or unless pious prayers to God prevent it. The kind of death is known from the nature of the sign in which they are conjoined. If they are conjoined in watery signs, death and danger are indicated by waters; in fiery signs, by iron, burning and fire; in earthy signs, by a fall from a height, ruin and the like; in airy signs, by strangling, suffocating catarrh, beheading and so on.

units.la: Octava sua natura infausta, Solem enim & reliquas stellas ad occasum tendentes, à conspectu nostro abripit, ut frui ipsarum amplius luce non possimus: cholerica est, meridionalis, fœminina: habet vesicam, genitalia, tenasmum, stranguriam. Saturnus hic est consignificator: dicitur etiam porta superna, unde scilicet Sol ad occasum tendens, veluti reclusis portis deducitur, vel quia stellis occasuris quasi fores aperit: judicium similiter ex hac sumitur de mortis qualitate, demortuorumq; hæreditatibus, timoribus, periculis vitam concernentibus, venenisq; ac facultatibus occultis.
units.tr: The eighth house is unfortunate by its nature, for it snatches the Sun and the other stars that are tending to set away from our sight, so that we can no longer enjoy their light. It is choleric, southern and feminine, and it governs the bladder, the genitals, tenesmus and strangury. Saturn is its co-signifier. It is also called the upper gate, either because the Sun, tending to set, is led down as though the gates had been thrown open, or because it opens the doors, as it were, for the stars that are about to set. Judgment is likewise drawn from it concerning the manner of death, the inheritances of the dead, fears, dangers that threaten life, poisons and hidden powers.

units.la: Nona sua natura bona, unde ex eventuum significatione, ad res divinas & religionem pertinentium, Dea dicitur, significat enim religionem, divinationem, sapientiam, somnia, itinera majora, & in his felicitatem vel pericula. Est cholerica, meridionalis fœminina: domus divina: habet epar cum coxarum medietate. In hac gaudet Sol, Jupiter est consignificator.
units.tr: The ninth house is good by its nature. From its signification of events pertaining to divine things and religion, it is called the Goddess, for it signifies religion, divination, wisdom, dreams and longer journeys, and in these either happiness or dangers. It is choleric, southern and feminine, a divine house, and it governs the liver and the half of the hips. The Sun rejoices in it, and Jupiter is its co-signifier.

units.la: Decima felix sua natura est, vocatur & medium, culmen, & summum cœli: item locus regius: sumitur enim ex ea judicium de honoribus, dignitatibus, gratia & favore magnatum, de Magistratibus, artis studiisque genere, officiis tam publicis quam privatis, tum etiam peculari statu matris: masculina est, sanguinea, meridionalis: habet coxarum partem inferiorem & genua. Consignificator est Mars.
units.tr: The tenth house is fortunate by its nature. It is also called the midheaven, the summit and the top of the heaven, and likewise the royal place. For judgment is drawn from it concerning honours, dignities, the favour and grace of great men, magistrates, the kind of art and study, public and private offices, and also the particular state of the mother. It is masculine, sanguine and southern, and it governs the lower part of the hips and the knees. Its co-signifier is Mars.

units.la: Undecima sua natura est bona, masculina, sanguinea, Orientalis, habet crura ad talos usque: Jupiter in ea gaudet cum consignificatore Sole. Sumitur ex ea judicium de amicitia, hominumq; favoribus.
units.tr: The eleventh house is good by its nature. It is masculine, sanguine and eastern, and it governs the legs down to the ankles. Jupiter rejoices in it, with the Sun as co-signifier. Judgment is drawn from it concerning friendship and the favour of men.

units.la: Duodecima, infausta sua natura & maligna, malus dæmon, ab infelicium eventuum, qui sæpe in ea contingunt, nomen sortita: masculina, sanguinea, Orientalis, habet pedes cum podagra: significat autem carceres, ærumnas, mœrorem, inimieos occultos, & odium : animalia item majora, ut equos, leo-nes,commodumq; ex his vel periculum. In hac malefici reperti cum luminari alterutro, inimicitias & captivitates plerumque portenderunt. Nec desunt exempla magnorum Heroum, qui-bus,si opus esset,id luculenter possem probare. Sed abrumpen-dus sermo est, & ad 4.coeli quadrantes dirigendus.
units.tr: The twelfth house is unfortunate and malign by its nature, an evil daemon, having received its name from the unlucky events that often happen in it. It is masculine, sanguine and eastern, and it governs the feet, with gout. It signifies prisons, hardships, sorrow, hidden enemies and hatred; also larger animals, such as horses and lions, and advantage or danger from them. Malefactors found in this house with either luminary have mostly portended enmities and captivities. Nor are examples of great heroes lacking, which I could clearly prove if there were need. But the discourse must be broken off here and directed to the four quadrants of the heaven.

units.la: Primus quadrans est,ab ascendente usq; ad medium coe-li,complectiturq; domum 10.11. & 12. Orientalis est,masculinus, puerilis, sanguineus, vernalis.
units.tr: The first quadrant runs from the ascendant up to the midheaven and embraces the 10th, 11th and 12th houses. It is eastern, masculine, boyish, sanguine and vernal.

units.la: Secundus à medio cœli est usq; in Occidentem, ut 9. 8. & 7. estq; meridianus,foemininus,cholericus,æstivus,juvenilis.
units.tr: The second quadrant runs from the midheaven to the west, that is, the 9th, 8th and 7th houses. It is southern, feminine, choleric, summery and youthful.

units.la: Tertius ab Occidente est usq; in angulum terræ, complectiturq; 6. 5. & 4. occidentalis est, masculinus, autumnalis,melancholicus,senilis.
units.tr: The third quadrant runs from the west to the angle of the earth and embraces the 6th, 5th and 4th houses. It is western, masculine, autumnal, melancholic and aged.

units.la: Quartus complectitur 3.2. & ascendens, estq; septentrio-nalis,foeminimus,phlegmaticus,hyemalis,defectivus.
units.tr: The fourth quadrant embraces the 3rd, 2nd and the ascendant. It is northern, feminine, phlegmatic, wintry and defective.

units.la: Cum hac divisione quadrantum fere congruit distinctio quatuor quadrantum zodiaci: circuli enim pars quarta, quæ est ab initio arietis usq; in geminorum finem, est calida & humida, vernalis, puerilis, sanguinea : à libra in capricornum, frigida & sicca, autumnalis, melancholica : à capricorno in pisces, frigida & humida, defectiva, hyemalis, phlegmatica : à cancro vero in libram usq;, calida & sicca, æstiva, cholerica. Medietates cœli quod attinet, medietas à medio cœli usque ad ascendens, & ab ascendente usque ad quartam, dicitur medietas ascendens, complectiturq; 10. 11. 12. 1. 2. & 3. domos : altera dicitur descendens, quam scilicet constituunt domus 9. 8. 7. 6. 5. & 4. In illa Planetæ constituti dicuntur esse in medietate ascendente, hic, in medietate descendente.
units.tr: This division into quadrants nearly agrees with the distinction of the four quadrants of the zodiac. For the fourth part of the circle that runs from the beginning of Aries to the end of Gemini is hot and moist, vernal, boyish and sanguine; from Libra to Capricorn it is cold and dry, autumnal and melancholic; from Capricorn to Pisces it is cold and moist, defective, wintry and phlegmatic; and from Cancer to Libra it is hot and dry, summery and choleric. As for the halves of the heaven, the half from the midheaven to the ascendant, and from the ascendant to the fourth house, is called the ascending half and embraces the 10th, 11th, 12th, 1st, 2nd and 3rd houses. The other is called the descending half, which is made up of the 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th, 5th and 4th houses. Planets placed in the former are said to be in the ascending half, and those in the latter in the descending half.

units.la: Atq; sic stellarum tam inerrantium, quàm errantium, seu Planetarum vires, naturæ, motus, proprietates & affectiones, signorum quoque divisiones, domiciliorum ac quadrantum-coeli distinctiones, significationesq;, ex probatissimis Astrono-mis, duce experientia, sensu praemonstrante viam, sunt, quanta potuit fieri brevitate & perspicuitate, collectae probeq; exploratae, restat, antequam ad alteram discursus hujus partem progrediar, ex hactenus praestratis, ac praecognitis, Planetarum et-iam dignitates & debilitates investigare, sine quarum exacta cognitione judicium Astrologicum tantum abest, ut veritatis aliquid contineat, ut etiam plane perversum dicendum sit. Ob-lato igitur themate aliquo natalitio, prima intentio & cura esse debet, utrum Planeta sit debilis vel fortis, nec hoc tantum-, verum etiam, quot habeat dignitates & debilitates, tum-, quis dignitatibus caeteros superet, is enim totius thematis Praeses, Dominus & director est proclamandus ac constituendus.
units.tr: And so the powers, natures, motions, properties and affections of the stars, both fixed and wandering (that is, the planets), the divisions of the signs, the distinctions of the houses and quadrants of the heaven, and their significations, have been gathered, as briefly and clearly as could be done, from the most approved astronomers, with experience as guide and the senses showing the way, and have been carefully tested. Before I proceed to the second part of this discourse, it remains, from what has been set out and previously established, to investigate also the dignities and debilities of the planets. Without an exact knowledge of these, astrological judgment is so far from containing any truth that it must even be called plainly perverse. Therefore, when some natal theme has been put forward, the first aim and care must be to determine whether a planet is weak or strong; and not only this, but also how many dignities and debilities it has, and which planet surpasses the others in dignities. For that planet is to be proclaimed and appointed the president, lord and director of the whole theme.

units.la: Dignitas est potestas, virtus, seu fortitudo Planetae, quam-habet seu accipit, vel ratione alicujus signi, vel ratione positus, motusq;, vel ratione aspectus, vel ratione stellarum fixarum, signo illi subjectarum, vel etiam propter occultam aliquam sympathian, cum scilicet in uno signo efficacior deprehenditur, quam in alio.
units.tr: Dignity is the power, virtue or strength of a planet, which it has or receives either by reason of some sign, or by reason of its position and motion, or by reason of an aspect, or by reason of the fixed stars subject to that sign, or even on account of some hidden sympathy, namely when it is found to be more effective in one sign than in another.

units.la: Ex dignitatibus autem omnibus, quinq; ex observationibus vocantur essentiales, πρῶτοι[?] οἰκοδεσποτικοί[?], ut domus, exaltationes, triplicitas, terminus & facies, οἶκοι, ὑψώματα, τριγώνῳ[?], ὅρια[?], φάσεις: reliquae dicuntur accidentales, ut directio, receptio, velocitas in motu, augmentum luminis, positus in domo 1.10.7.4.2.5. ascensio in circulo augis, ascensio in Septentriones, in trigono Jovis vel Veneris, in Sextili Jovis vel Veneris, corporalis conjunctio Jovis Venerisve, existentia inter duas fortunas, securitas, &c. quibus omnibus debilitates opponuntur. Exordienda autem fortitudinum & debilitatum harum determinatio a luminaribus est, quorum potissima in omni themate genethliaco habenda est ratio, idq; propter luminis efficaciam, radiorumq; efficaciorem projectum.
units.tr: Of all the dignities, five are called essential from observation: the lordships of the houses [οἶκοι], as the domicile, the exaltations [ὑψώματα], the triplicity [τριγώνῳ], the term [ὅρια] and the face [φάσεις]. The rest are called accidental, such as direction, reception, speed in motion, increase of light, position in the 1st, 10th, 7th, 4th, 2nd or 5th house, ascension in the circle of the augis, ascension in the Septentriones, being in the trine of Jupiter or Venus, in the sextile of Jupiter or Venus, bodily conjunction with Jupiter or Venus, existence between two fortunes, security, and so on. To all of these debilities are opposed. The determination of these strengths and weaknesses must begin with the luminaries, of which the principal must be taken into account in every genethliacal theme, and this on account of the efficacy of light and the more effective projection of the rays.

units.la: Primò igitur, quando Sol fortunet, quando infortunet, & quando fortificet, inquirendum. Ubi tenendum, omnia, quæ fortunant, etiam fortificare, & omnia, quæ infortunant, etiam debilitare.
units.tr: First, therefore, it must be inquired when the Sun fortunes, when it infortunes, and when it fortifies. Here it must be held that all things that fortune also fortify, and all things that infortune also debilitate.

units.la: Fortunat Sol, si fuerit in conjunctione, vel bono aspectu, hoc est, trigono vel sextili fortunæ, ut Jovis vel Veneris,
units.tr: The Sun is fortunate if it is in conjunction, or in a good aspect, that is, a trine or sextile, with a fortune such as Jupiter or Venus;

units.la: Obsessus à fortunis, vel eorum radiis, ut si Sol esset in 15.gr. cancri, Jupiter in 6.cancri, & Venus in 21.cancri, Sol utrinq; obsideretur à fortunis.
units.tr: or if it is beset by the fortunes or their rays, as when the Sun is in the 15th degree of Cancer, Jupiter in the 6th of Cancer, and Venus in the 21st of Cancer, so that the Sun is beset on both sides by fortunes.

units.la: Si mali ab eo cadant, & tunc Solem oportet esse vel in angulo, vel succedente: In bono aspectu Lunæ. In aliqua suarum dignitatum essentialium: Separatus ab infortuna, & junctus fortunæ. Receptus ex domicilio vel exaltatione, ut si Sol esset in cancro, domicilio Lunæ, & Luna in leone, domicilio Solis, diceretur Sol à Luna receptus ex domicilio. Item: Sol in in tauro, & Luna in ariete, recipiunt se mutuò ex exaltatione, nam in tauro exaltatur Luna, in ariete vero Sol, qui fortificare tunc dicitur, si fuerit Ascendens in eccentrico. In superiori parte eccentrici. In angulo, vel succedente: In signo & quarta masculina, exceptâ libra: Propè Jovem vel Venerem: In dignitatibus Jovis vel Veneris. Elevatus supra infortunas.
units.tr: It is also fortunate if the malefics fall away from it. The Sun should then be in an angle or a succedent house; in a good aspect of the Moon; in one of its essential dignities; separated from an infortune and joined to a fortune; received by domicile or exaltation, as when the Sun is in Cancer, the domicile of the Moon, and the Moon is in Leo, the domicile of the Sun, and so the Sun is said to be received by the Moon through domicile. Likewise, when the Sun is in Taurus and the Moon in Aries, they receive each other through exaltation, for the Moon is exalted in Taurus and the Sun in Aries. The Sun is said to be strengthened then if it is ascendant in the eccentric; in the upper part of the eccentric; in an angle or succedent house; in a masculine sign and quarter, except Libra; near Jupiter or Venus; in the dignities of Jupiter or Venus; and raised above the infortunes.

units.la: Idem vero infortunat, si fuerit Conjunctus infortunæ, vel in ejus malo aspectu: Obsessus ab infortunis, vel ipsorum radiis. In malo aspectu Lunæ vel aliorum. In casu vel detrimento Separatus à fortuna, seu recedens ab ea, & infortunæ ap-plicans. Cum cauda draconis.
units.tr: Conversely, the Sun is unfortunate if it is conjoined with an infortune or in its evil aspect; beset by the infortunes or their rays; in an evil aspect of the Moon or of the others; in its fall or detriment; separated from a fortune, or moving away from one and applying to an infortune; or with the dragon's tail.

units.la: Debilitat autem, si fuerit Descendens in circulo augis. In inferiori parte eccentrici. In domo cadente. In signo & quarta fœmininis. In dignitatibus infortunarum. Infortuna elevata supra eum. Peregrinus, id est, cùm non existit in aliqua suarum digni-tatum. Non receptus Conjunctus Planetæ existenti in casu vel detrimento suo.
units.tr: It is weakened if it is descending in the circle of the apogee; in the lower part of the eccentric; in a cadent house; in a feminine sign and quarter; in the dignities of the infortunes; with an infortune raised above it; peregrine, that is, when it is not in any of its dignities; not received; or conjoined with a planet that is in its fall or detriment.

units.la: Habet autem Saturnus detrimentum suum in cancro & leone: casum in ariete.
units.tr: Saturn has its detriment in Cancer and Leo, and its fall in Aries.

units.la: Jupiter detrimentum habet in geminis & virgine, cadit autem in capricorno, nam in cancro exaltatur, unde præceden-ti & hoc anno Jupiter fuit in sua exaltatione, videlicet cancro, in quo magnarum est virium.
units.tr: Jupiter has its detriment in Gemini and Virgo and falls in Capricorn, for it is exalted in Cancer; hence in the preceding year, and this year as well, Jupiter was in its exaltation, namely in Cancer, in which it is of great power.

units.la: Mars detrimentum capit in libra & tauro, sed cadit in cancro.
units.tr: Mars has its detriment in Libra and Taurus, but falls in Cancer.

units.la: Sol detrimentum patitur in aquario, casum in libra.
units.tr: The Sun suffers detriment in Aquarius and falls in Libra.

units.la: Venus detrimentum capessit in scorpione & ariete, cadit in virgine.
units.tr: Venus has its detriment in Scorpio and Aries and falls in Virgo.

units.la: Mercurius detrimentum habet in piscibus (in quibus etiam, nisi à Venere juvetur, plane eum reddidisse stupidos, compertum habetur) & sagittario, casum in iisdem piscibus, nam-in in virgine domicilium habet, & exaltationem simul, unde etiam maxime hoc signo gaudet. Lunae detrimentum est in capricorno, casus in scorpione. Porro Luna dicitur fortunare, si fuerit Coniuncta fortunae, vel in aspectu. Obsessa a fortunis, vel radiis earundem. Si malefici cadant ab ea. In bono aspectu Solis, vel aliorum. In aliqua suarum dignitatum. Separata ab infortuna. Recepta ex domicilio vel exaltatione.
units.tr: Mercury has its detriment in Pisces (in which, unless it is helped by Venus, it is known to make people quite stupid) and in Sagittarius; it falls in those same Pisces, for it has its domicile and exaltation together in Virgo, and so it especially rejoices in that sign. The Moon's detriment is in Capricorn and its fall in Scorpio. The Moon is said to be fortunate if it is conjoined with a fortune or in its aspect; beset by fortunes or their rays; when the malefics fall away from it; in a good aspect of the Sun or others; in one of its dignities; separated from an infortune; and received by domicile or exaltation.

units.la: Unita Soli, seu in Cazymi. In corde Solis Planeta esse dici-tur, cum fuerit Soli proximus intra 16. minuta ante vel post, id est, cum distat a Sole secundum longitudinem & latitudinem 16. tantum minutis, ut, si Sol esset in 15. gradu cancri, 38. min. Luna similiter in 15. gradu, min. 38. Luna diceretur esse in Cazymi seu corde Solis. Infortuna re Lunam compertum est, si fuerit Juncta infortunae, vel corpore, vel per radiaturam. Obsessa ab infortunis, vel radiatura earum. In malo aspectu Solis vel aliorum. In opposito suarum dignitatum. Separata a fortunis. Juncta stellis fixis maleficis, ut cordi scorpionis in 3. gr. sa-gittarii, capiti Medusae in 23. gr. tauri, &c. Non demum recepta. Fortificare autem dicitur, si fuerit Septentrionalis. Ascendens in eccentrico. Ascendens in epicyclo. Nuper egressa ex radiis Solis. In angulo vel succedente. Occidentalis à Sole. In signo & quarta fœmininis. In termino beneficarum. Elevata supra infortunas. In dignitatibus fortunarum. Cursu velox. Noctu supra terram, die vero infra terram.
units.tr: The Moon is united with the Sun, or is in the cazimi. A planet is said to be in the heart of the Sun when it is within 16 minutes of the Sun before or after, that is, when it is distant from the Sun by only 16 minutes in longitude and latitude; so if the Sun is in the 15th degree of Cancer at 38 minutes, the Moon likewise at 15 degrees, 38 minutes, would be said to be in the cazimi, or heart of the Sun. It is known that the Moon is made unfortunate if it is joined to an infortune, either by body or by ray; beset by infortunes or their rays; in an evil aspect of the Sun or others; in the opposite of its dignities; separated from the fortunes; joined to evil fixed stars, such as the heart of Scorpio at 3 degrees of Sagittarius, or the head of Medusa at 23 degrees of Taurus, and so on; and finally not received. It is said to be strengthened if it is northern; ascendant in the eccentric; ascendant in the epicycle; recently emerged from the Sun's rays; in an angle or succedent house; western from the Sun; in a feminine sign and quarter; in the term of the benefics; raised above the infortunes; in the dignities of the fortunes; swift in motion; and, by night above the earth, by day below it.

units.la: Eadem debilitat, si fuerit Peregrina. Meridionalis. Descendens in eccentrico & epicyclo. Sub radiis, & combusta. In domo cadente. In signo & quarta masculina. Noctu infra terram, die supra terram. Si infortunæ elevantur supra eam.
units.tr: The same planet is weakened if it is peregrine; southern; descending in the eccentric or epicycle; under the Sun's rays and combust; in a cadent house; in a masculine sign and quarter; by night below the earth and by day above it; or if the infortunes are raised above it.

units.la: In via combusta, ut in Septentrione à 18. geminorum, ad 2. cancri, in meridie vero ab 8. sagittarii, in 13. ejusdem, iterumq; à 24. sagittarii, usq; in 2. capricorni. In geminis. In dignitatibus infortunarum. In conjunctione Planetæ cadentis ab angulo.
units.tr: In the combust way, namely in the northern course from 18 Gemini to 2 Cancer, and in the southern from 8 Sagittarius to 13 Sagittarius, and again from 24 Sagittarius to 2 Capricorn; in Gemini; in the dignities of the infortunes; or in conjunction with a planet that is falling from an angle.

units.la: In conjunctione Planetæ existentis in opposito suarum dignitatum. Tarda in motu.
units.tr: In conjunction with a planet that is in the opposite of its dignities; slow in motion.

units.la: Sed Saturnus, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercurius fortunant, si fuerint Conjuncti fortunis, vel in harum radiatura. Obsessi à fortunis, vel earundem radiis. Uniti Soli, vel in ejus bono aspectu. In bono aspectu Lunæ. In aliqua suarum dignitatum. Veloces cursu. Aucti lumine. Directi. Recepti. Infortunant, si fuerint Conjuncti infortunatis stellis. Obsessi ab infortunis, vel radiis earundem. Combusti. In malo aspectu Lunæ vel Solis. In oppositosuarum dignitatum. In domo cadente. Separati à fortunatis. Minuti lumine. In terminis malorum. Peregrini. Retrogradi. Cum capite vel cauda intra 12. gradus. Fortificant iidem, si fuerint In angulo vel succedente, excepta octava. Ascendentes in septentrionem. Ascendentes in eccentrico. In statione secunda. Elongantes è radiis solaribus.
units.tr: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury are fortunate if they are conjoined with fortunes or in their ray; beset by fortunes or their rays; united with the Sun or in its good aspect; in a good aspect of the Moon; in one of their dignities; swift in course; increased in light; direct; and received. They are unfortunate if they are conjoined with unfortunate stars; beset by infortunes or their rays; combust; in an evil aspect of the Moon or the Sun; in the opposite of their dignities; in a cadent house; separated from the fortunate planets; diminished in light; in the terms of the malefics; peregrine; or retrograde; or with the head or tail within 12 degrees. The same planets are strengthened if they are in an angle or succedent house, except the eighth; ascendant in the north; ascendant in the eccentric; in the second station; or moving away from the Sun's rays.

units.la: Orientales à Sole, sed Mercurius & Venus à Sole occidentales. (Orientalitas secundum Ptolomæum est duplex, vel respectu horizontis, vel respectu Solis. Respectu horizontis Planetæ Orientales dicuntur ab Oriente usq; ad medium cœli. Occidentales à medio cœli usq; in angulum & cuspidem Occidentalem. Respectu autem Solis, Planetæ dicuntur Orientales, qui præcedunt manè Solem in Oriente. Occidentales, qui Solem Occidentem vesperi insequuntur. Deinde tres superiores, Saturnus, Jupiter, Mars, à conjunctione ipsorum cum Sole usq; ad oppositionem eorundem sunt Orientales, ob oppositione vero ad conjunctionem, Occidentales. Venus autem & Mercurius, quamdiu Solem Occidentem insequuntur, Occidentales, praecedentes Orientem mane, Orientales.)
units.tr: Planets are oriental of the Sun, but Mercury and Venus are western of the Sun. (According to Ptolemy, orientality is twofold, either with respect to the horizon or with respect to the Sun. With respect to the horizon, planets are called oriental from the East up to the midheaven, and western from the midheaven up to the western angle and cusp. With respect to the Sun, planets are called oriental if they precede the Sun in the morning in the East, and western if they follow the setting Sun in the evening. Then the three superior planets, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars, are oriental from their conjunction with the Sun up to their opposition, and western from opposition to conjunction. Venus and Mercury, as long as they follow the setting Sun, are western, and oriental when they precede the rising Sun in the morning.)

units.la: In signis & quartis masculinis, sed Mercurius & Venus in signis & quartis foemininis.
units.tr: They are in signs and masculine quarters; but Mercury and Venus are in feminine signs and quarters.

units.la: In die supra terram, noctu vero sub terra, sed Mars, Venus & Mercurius die sub terra, noctu vero supra terras.
units.tr: By day above the earth, and by night below the earth; but Mars, Venus and Mercury are below the earth by day, and above the earth by night.

units.la: In dignitatibus fortunarum.
units.tr: In the dignities of the fortunes.

units.la: Saturnus, Jupiter, Mars, elevati supra Mercurium & Venerem, hi vero supra Lunam.
units.tr: Saturn, Jupiter and Mars are raised above Mercury and Venus, and these in turn above the Moon.

units.la: Debilitare deprehenduntur, si fuerint
units.tr: They are found to be weakened if they are

units.la: Descendentes in meridiem:
units.tr: descending towards the South;

units.la: In statione prima.
units.tr: in the first station;

units.la: Descendentes in circulo augis.
units.tr: descending in the circle of the apogee;

units.la: Occidentales à Sole, sed Mercurius & Venus à Sole Orientales.
units.tr: western of the Sun, but Mercury and Venus are oriental of the Sun;

units.la: In signis & quartis foemininis, sed Mercurius & Venus in masculinis.
units.tr: in feminine signs and quarters, but Mercury and Venus in masculine ones;

units.la: In via combusta.
units.tr: in the combust way;

units.la: In die sub terra, noctu supra terram, sed Mars, Venus, Mercurius, die supra, noctu infra terram.
units.tr: by day below the earth and by night above it, but Mars, Venus and Mercury by day above and by night below the earth;

units.la: Conjuncti Planetae retrogrado.
units.tr: conjoined with a retrograde planet;

units.la: Conjuncti Planetae impedito.
units.tr: conjoined with an impeded planet;

units.la: Conjuncti Planetae cadenti.
units.tr: conjoined with a falling planet;

units.la: Non recepti.
units.tr: not received.

units.la: Si infortunae elevantur[?] supra alios. Verum ut haec omnia facilius percipi, memoriaque comprehendi queant, praestat, totam hanc observationem de fortitudinibus & debilitatibus Planetarum, numeris distinguere, atque ita judicare, quis Planetarum alterum dignitatibus vel debilitatibus superet: qui enim plures habuerit dignitates, is fortissimus & fortunatissimus cencensendus est, qui plures debilitates, debilissimus, semper enim dignitatum testimonia atque suffragia cum debilitatibus sunt conferenda. Exempli gratiâ: Domus prima vel 10. obtinet dignitates 5. Planeta igitur in aliqua harum domorum repertus, 5. habet dignitates, & totidem si fuerit in domicilio proprio, ratione scilicet signi, &c. Rem omnem exhibet sequens tabella.
units.tr: If the infortunes are raised above the others. But so that all these things may be more easily grasped and held in memory, it is better to distinguish this whole observation of the strengths and weaknesses of the planets by numbers, and so to judge which of the planets surpasses another in dignities or debilities. For whoever has more dignities is to be reckoned the strongest and most fortunate, and whoever has more debilities the weakest, since the testimonies and suffrages of the dignities must always be weighed against the debilities. For example: the first or tenth house holds five dignities. A planet found in one of these houses therefore has five dignities, and as many if it is in its own domicile, by reason of the sign, and so on. The following table sets out the whole matter.

units.la: Fortitudines Planetarum.
units.tr: Strengths of the Planets.

Prior arietis decas, cōtinens priores 10. gradus, tribuitur Marti, secunda Soli, tertia Veneri. Mars igitur existens in ariete, & quidem intra 10. gradum, est in facie sua. Idem judicium de cæteris. Applicatio cum fortuna ex sextili | 3. Receptio | 5. Gaudium ratione signi | 3. Gaudium ratione domus cœli | 2. Orientalitas trium superiorum | 2. Occidentalitas inferiorum | 2. Hayz seu conformitas | 3. In hayz Planeta dicitur esse, cum diurnus in die supra terram, noctu vero sub terra, & Planeta nocturnus die sub terra, nocte supra terram est, ut Saturnus, Sol, Jupiter, Mercurius, Planetae diurni de die existentes supra terram, de nocte vero sub terra, sunt in suo hayz, id est, conformitate. Mars vero, Venus & Luna Planetae no-cturni, sunt in suo hayz, cum in diurna genitura sub terra, in no-cturna vero supra terram sunt. Sic in hayz Planeta esse dicitur, cum masculinus in signo & quarta masculinis, & orientalis, foe-mininus in signo & quarta foeminínis, & occidentalis extiterit.
units.tr: Every sign has three decans, which they call faces, and each decan contains 10 degrees. For example, the first decan of Aries, which contains the first 10 degrees, is assigned to Mars, the second to the Sun, and the third to Venus. So Mars in Aries, and indeed within the 10th degree, is in its own face. The same judgment applies to the others. In the 1st or 10th house of heaven | 5. In the 7th or 4th | 4. In the 9th, 11th or 5th | 3. In the 3rd | 1. Being in Cazimi | 5. Bodily conjunction with a fortune | 5. Application with a fortune by trine | 4. Application with a fortune by sextile | 3. Reception | 5. Joy by reason of sign | 3. Joy by reason of house of heaven | 2. Orientality of the three superior planets | 2. Occidentality of the inferior planets | 2. Hayz, or conformity | 3. A planet is said to be in hayz when a diurnal planet is above the earth by day and below it by night, and a nocturnal planet is below the earth by day and above it by night. Saturn, Sun, Jupiter and Mercury are diurnal planets: when they are above the earth by day and below it by night, they are in their own hayz, that is, in conformity. Mars, Venus and Luna are nocturnal planets: they are in their own hayz when, in a diurnal nativity, they are below the earth, and in a nocturnal nativity, above the earth. Thus a planet is said to be in hayz when a masculine planet is in a masculine sign and a masculine quarter and is oriental, or when a feminine planet is in a feminine sign and a feminine quarter and is occidental.

units.la: Masculini autem Planetae sunt Saturnus, Jupiter, Mars, Sol, foeminini Venus & Luna: Mercurius cum masculinis masculinus, cum foemininis foemininus est: Signa masculina sunt, aries, gemini, leo, libra, sagittarius, aquarius, caetera foeminina. Quartae deniq; coeli masculinae sunt, 10. 11. 12. 4. 5. & 6. foemininae, 1. 2. 3. 7. 8. 9. alias dicitur conformitas quartae, in qua Planeta esse dicitur, si diurnus supra terram, vel nocturnus infra terram, mas-culinusq; in signo & quarta masculinis fuerit inventus, quod tamen rarum est, quamvis non raro in suo sit hayz, id est, con-formitatum aliqua. In conformitate quartae | 3. Securitas | 5.
units.tr: The masculine planets are Saturn, Jupiter, Mars and the Sun; the feminine are Venus and the Moon; Mercury is masculine with the masculine planets and feminine with the feminine. The masculine signs are Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius and Aquarius; the rest are feminine. Finally, the masculine quarters of the heaven are the 10th, 11th, 12th, 4th, 5th and 6th houses, and the feminine are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 7th, 8th and 9th. Elsewhere there is said to be conformity of quarter, in which a planet is said to be when it is diurnal above the earth, or nocturnal below it, and is found masculine in a masculine sign and quarter. This is rare, though not uncommonly a planet is in its own hayz, that is, in some kind of conformity. In conformity of quarter | 3. Security | 5.

Directio | 4. Velocitas cursus | 2. Augmentum luminis | 1. Ascensio in eccentrico | 2. Ascensio in Septentriones | 2.
units.tr: A planet is said to be secure when there are 60 degrees between it and the Sun on the eastern side, and also when it is wholly free from the rays of malefic planets and violent fixed stars. Direction | 4. Speed of motion | 2. Increase of light | 1. Ascension in the eccentric | 2. Ascension toward the northern regions | 2.

units.la: Decrescens 3. Verum Johannes Hispalensis generaliora tantum ex dignitatibus & debilitatibus hisce observat, quem etiam Neoterici pleriq; omnes sequuntur. Primò enim considerat, an Planeta sit in aliqua suarum dignitatum, nec ne? Secundò, an in bono cœli loco? Tertiò, an directus? Quartò, an liber à radiis Solis? Quintò, an motu velox, an verò tardus? Sextò, an fortunæ applicet, vel infortunæ, & si applicet, qua radiatura? His ego addo stellas fixas, non enim sufficit scire, quomodo, id est, in quo loco figuræ seu thematis cœlestis collocetur, sed vel omnium maximè interest perpendere, quas sibi habeat adjunctas stellas firmamenti, & quidem ex his insigniores, ut oculum tauri, capita geminorum, cor leonis, caudâ ejusdem, spicam virginis, Arcturum, canem majorem seu sirium, Procyonem, cor scorpii, orionis humeros, orionis cingulum, pedem ejusdem sinistrum, lances, extremam in aqua fusa, lyræ fidiculam, cor aquilæ, caput Medusæ, hircum, 7. in ursa majori lucidam hydræ, lucidam coronæ, &c. His enim Planetarum vires augeri atque extimulari, experimentis quotidianis habetur patefactum. Quanto igitur plura Planeta habuerit testimonia dignitatum, tanto erit fortunatior, & contra, tanto infortunatior, quò debilior, quanto scilicet numerus debilitatum, numerum dignitatum magis superat.
units.tr: Decreasing, 3. But John of Seville observes only the more general matters among these dignities and debilities, and most of the moderns follow him. First he considers whether the planet is in one of its dignities or not; second, whether it is in a good place of the heaven; third, whether it is direct; fourth, whether it is free from the rays of the Sun; fifth, whether it is swift in motion or rather slow; sixth, whether it applies to a fortune or to an infortune, and if it applies, with what kind of ray. To these I add the fixed stars. For it is not enough to know how a planet is placed, that is, in what place of the figure or celestial theme it stands; it matters most of all to weigh which stars of the firmament are joined to it, and especially the more notable of these: the eye of the Bull, the heads of the Twins, the heart of the Lion, the tail of the same, the Spica of Virgo, Arcturus, the Greater Dog or Sirius, Procyon, the heart of the Scorpion, the shoulders of Orion, the belt of Orion, his left foot, the Scales, the last star in the Water poured out, the string of the Lyre, the heart of the Eagle, the head of Medusa, the Goat, the seventh star in the Great Bear, the bright star of the Hydra, the bright star of the Crown, etc. For it has been made plain by daily experience that the powers of the planets are increased and stirred up by these. Therefore, the more testimonies of dignity a planet has, the more fortunate it will be, and conversely, the more unfortunate, the weaker it is, namely, the more its number of debilities exceeds its number of dignities.

units.la: Cuspides, id est, initia domiciliorum cœli sua quoque habent fortunia & infortunia: fortunantur enim per conjunctionem, & omnes aspectus bonorum Planetarum, & per bonos aspectus Planetarum mediocrium, cùm eadem loca aspiciunt, vel illis juncti fuerint ex medietate, vel intra medietatem orbium suorum: ut si 14. tauri gradus esset cuspis primæ domus in figura cœli, & Jupiter esset in 23. gr. tauri, tunc Jupiter ex medietate dictate orbis sui, quæ est 9. graduum, fortunaret cuspidem primæ domus: & hoc idem efficeret in quolibet gradu intermedio, seu interjecto inter 23. & 14. Pari ratione aspectus sunt observandi, ut sit 14. gradus tauri, ut prius, cuspis primæ domus, & Jupiter in 23. gradu virginis, aspiciens cuspidem ex trigono & medietate orbis sui, iterum fortunatur cuspis primæ ex triquetra Jovis radiatura: quod si vero Planetæ mali per conjunctionem, quadratū, aut oppositum, cuspidibus applicuerint, infortunant etiam & debilitant illas.
units.tr: The cusps, that is, the beginnings of the houses of heaven, also have their own fortunes and infortunes. For they are fortified by conjunction and by all the aspects of the benefic planets, and by the good aspects of the lesser planets, when these aspect the same places, or are joined to them within half of their orbs, or within the half of their own orbs. For example, if the 14th degree of Taurus were the cusp of the first house in the figure of heaven, and Jupiter were at the 23rd degree of Taurus, then Jupiter, within half of its said orb, which is 9 degrees, would fortify the cusp of the first house; and it would do the same at any intermediate degree lying between 23 and 14. By the same reasoning the aspects are to be observed: if the 14th degree of Taurus, as before, is the cusp of the first house, and Jupiter is at the 23rd degree of Virgo, aspecting the cusp by trine and within half of its orb, then again the cusp of the first house is fortified by the triangular ray of Jupiter. But if malefic planets have applied to the cusps by conjunction, square or opposition, they also infortune and weaken them.

units.la: Hic vero cuspidum domini, ipsiusq; genituræ seu figuræ Rectores inquirendi. Dominus cuspidis est, qui in illo signo, quod cuspidi adhæret, habet domicilium, vel qui in illo signo signiq; gradu plures habet dignitates, ut, si in cuspide orientali esset aries, Mars diceretur dominus ascendentis, quia aries ejus domicilium est: si secundam domum occuparet taurus, Venus esset Domina ibidem, quia in tauro habet suum domicilium: quoniam vero in ariete Sol habet exaltationem, & in tauro Luna suam, Mars assumit Solem in dominii participationem, & Venus similiter Lunam: & sic de cæteris quoque erit judicandum.
units.tr: Here, moreover, the lords of the cusps must be sought, and the rulers of the nativity or figure itself. The lord of a cusp is the one who has its domicile in the sign adjoining the cusp, or the one who has more dignities in that sign and degree. For example, if Aries were on the eastern cusp, Mars would be called lord of the ascendant, because Aries is his domicile. If Taurus occupied the second house, Venus would be its lady, because she has her domicile in Taurus. But since the Sun has its exaltation in Aries, and the Moon its own in Taurus, Mars takes the Sun into partnership of lordship, and Venus likewise the Moon. And so the same must be judged of the others.

units.la: Totius autem genituræ Dominus est, qui supra omnes alios Planetas elevatus, plures habet dignitates tàm essentiales, quàm accidentales: quod si vero nullus Planetarum ad dominium hoc suscipiendum reperiatur aptus, id est, neq; in medio cœli, neq; in ii.[?] neq; in 9. neq; etiam in essentialibus dignitatibus, vide locum Solis, locum Lunæ, ascendentis, partis fortunæ, & locum conjunctionis vel oppositionis luminarium, nativitatem proximè præcedentis, vide etiam Planetas his locis dominantes, & quicunq; in his quinque dictis locis plures habuerit dignitates essentiales, ut in domo, exaltatione, triplicitate, termino & facie, is totius thematis Dominus & victor constituendus est: quod si autem contigerit, ut sæpè fit, ut plures obtinens digni-tates infra terram sit, & in malo cœli loco, tunc is eligendus, qui dignitatum testimoniis & suffragiis proximè ei succedit: ut sit in figura alicujus locus Solis 11. gradus arietis: locus Lunæ 19. grad. scorpionis: ascendens 26. virginis. Partis fortunæ 4. tauri: oppositionis nativitatem proximè præcedentis 8. gradus arie-tis: collectis dignitatibus, invenio Martem in his quinq; locis obtinere dignitates 24. Saturnum 6. Jovem nullam, Solem 16. Venerem 14. Mercurium 13. Lunam 13. Victorem igitur hujus nativitatis pronuncio Martem cum Sole, qui præter dictas dignitates in quinque præcipuis locis etiam in perfecta & amica-bili cum Marte mixtione plurima in Solarem amicitiam convertet.
units.tr: The lord of the whole nativity or figure is the one who, elevated above all other planets, has more dignities, both essential and accidental. But if no planet is found fit to take up this lordship, that is, neither in the midheaven, nor in the [?] nor in the 9th, nor even in the essential dignities, then look to the place of the Sun, the place of the Moon, the ascendant, the Lot of Fortune, and the place of the conjunction or opposition of the luminaries that immediately preceded the nativity; look also to the planets ruling in these places. Whichever planet has more essential dignities in these five said places, such as in domicile, exaltation, triplicity, term and face, is to be established as lord of the whole theme and its victor. But if it happens, as it often does, that the planet with more dignities is below the earth and in a bad place of the heaven, then the one to be chosen is the one who next follows it in the testimonies and support of dignities. For example: in a certain figure the place of the Sun is 11 degrees of Aries, the place of the Moon 19 degrees of Scorpio, the ascendant 26 degrees of Virgo, the Lot of Fortune 4 degrees of Taurus, and the opposition of the nativity immediately preceding 8 degrees of Aries. Having collected the dignities, I find that Mars holds 24 dignities in these five places, Saturn 6, Jupiter none, the Sun 16, Venus 14, Mercury 13, and the Moon 13. Therefore I declare Mars with the Sun to be the victor of this nativity, since, besides the said dignities in the five principal places, Mars, in a perfect and friendly mixture with the Sun, will also turn much of its force into solar friendship.

units.la: Est enim Planetarum certus inter se consensus vel dissensus. Primò amici Jovis sunt omnes præterquam Mars. Veneris quoq; omnes, præter Saturnum. Saturni amici sunt Jupiter, Sol, Luna: Inimici Mars & Venus. Amica Martis Venus: Inimici ejus omnes, magis tamen Jupiter. Solis amici sunt Jupiter & Venus: Inimici Mars, Mercurius; Luna. Amici Mercurii, Jupiter, Venus, Saturnus: Inimici Sol, Luna, Mars. Amici Lunæ, Jupiter, Venus, Saturnus: Inimici Mars & Mercurius. Amici capitis draconis sunt Jupiter, Venus: Inimici Sol & Luna. Amici caudæ sunt Saturnus & Mars: Inimici Sol, Luna, Jupiter & Venus.
units.tr: There is a fixed agreement or disagreement among the planets. First, Jupiter is friendly to all except Mars, and Venus is friendly to all except Saturn. Saturn's friends are Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon; his enemies are Mars and Venus. Venus is Mars's friend, and all the others are his enemies, Jupiter most of all. The Sun's friends are Jupiter and Venus; his enemies are Mars, Mercury and the Moon. Mercury's friends are Jupiter, Venus and Saturn; his enemies are the Sun, the Moon and Mars. The Moon's friends are Jupiter, Venus and Saturn; her enemies are Mars and Mercury. The friends of the Dragon's Head are Jupiter and Venus; its enemies are the Sun and the Moon. The friends of the Dragon's Tail are Saturn and Mars; its enemies are the Sun, the Moon, Jupiter and Venus.

units.la: Ratione verò concordantiæ in natura, substantia, qualitate, & potestate amicitiam fovent, Mars & Sol, Jupiter & Venus, Venus & Luna. Sed inimici ratione domorum sunt Saturnus & Luna, Saturnus & Sol, Jupiter & Mercurius, Mars & Venus: Ratione exaltationis inimici sunt Saturnus & Sol, Jupiter & Mars, Venus & Mercurius. Ex quibus patet, perpetuam esse inimicitiam inter Solem & Saturnum, unde malum in omni genitura est,si Soli,præsertim si vitæ potestatem & dominium quod-dam sibi vendicat,à Saturno vel conjunctionalis, vel quadratus, vel oppositus radius infligatur. Saturnus enim cum Sole patri-monii & facultatum dissipationem, laboremq; ac damnum in-facultatibus acquirendis minatur, præsertim si fuerint ambo infra terram, quin etiam vitæ pericula decernit, adversasq; va-letudines frigidas, paralyticas, dignitatum jacturam, inimici-tias. Sed oppositio Solem radio Saturnus feriens substantiæ dis-sipationem, diurnas angustias, malam & difficilem minitatur mortem, noctuq; omnia erunt graviora, & in signis fœmininis. Itaq; in omni genitura seu nativitate prima debet esse fere cura, inquirere, an Saturnus Soli applicet, & qua radiatură.
units.tr: By agreement in nature, substance, quality and power, they foster friendship: Mars and the Sun, Jupiter and Venus, Venus and the Moon. But by their houses they are enemies: Saturn and the Moon, Saturn and the Sun, Jupiter and Mercury, Mars and Venus. By their exaltations they are enemies: Saturn and the Sun, Jupiter and Mars, Venus and Mercury. From these things it is clear that there is a perpetual enmity between the Sun and Saturn. Hence in every nativity there is evil, especially if Saturn, by conjunction, square or opposition, strikes the Sun with his ray, when the Sun claims for itself the power of life and a certain dominion. For Saturn, joined with the Sun, threatens the dissipation of property and resources, labour and loss in acquiring wealth, especially if both are below the earth; indeed he also determines dangers to life, unfavourable cold and paralytic illnesses, loss of dignities, and enmities. But when Saturn strikes the Sun with an opposing ray, it threatens the dissipation of substance, lasting distress, and a bad and difficult death; and at night all things will be harder, especially in feminine signs. Therefore, in every genethliacal chart or nativity, the first concern should be to inquire whether Saturn applies to the Sun, and by what ray.

units.la: Hactenus igitur de prima astralis scientiæ parte, videlicet Astronomia, quâ nunc valere jussa, ad alteram, quæ divinatrix di-citur, & μαντικὴ, sermonem converto. Hic verò ingentem adver-sus me turbâ Astrologiæ mastigum sum concitaturus. Itaq; scu-to Herculis clava, & Ariete opus est. Verùm adversarii non sunt tanti, ut auxiliatrices contra eos sint conscribendæ copiæ. Vos, Auditores, pro judicio & prudentia vestra judicate. Si quid pro-tulero, quod auribus vestris forsan videbitur asperius, leniam, si veritati quid detractum, corrigam, si verò dixero verum, no-lite succensere. Multi autem eruditi homines hanc astrorum scientiæ partem magnis sunt voluminibus insectati. Est in ma-nibus hominum, farrago criminationum à Pico non scripta, sed excerpta ex vetustioribus commentariis, qui ad hujus divina-tricis reprehensionem multò ante fuerunt collecti. Hos refuta-runt Bellantius, & alii quidam viri eruditi. Multæ autem leves & insulsæ cavillationes objiciuntur, quarum repetitio longior, & refutatio non est necessaria. Et si verum dicere liceat, mise-rum Astrologorum flagellum fuit Picus Mirandulanus, vir alio-quin eruditissimus, qui argumentis undiq; coacervatis artem incognitam & non intellectam publicè insectatus est, atq; dam-mnavit. Hoccine verò est ingenui hominis, exagitare publicè id quod nunquam vel noverit, vel intellexerit, &c. O tempora! sed & Neoterici quidam, qui publicis scriptis in hanc artem sunt invecti, sua exillo spicula deprompserunt, eò quidem acerbiora & virulentiora, quò quisq; est hujus divinæ artis imperitior, nam inter mundi jam jam ruituri morbos grassatur inprimis hoc ulcus, ut, qui sua etiam sponte ignorantiam artis profitentur, nihilominus tamen sibi persuadeant incognita se refutare posse, quia scilicet judicant esse falsa, cùm ridiculum sit, falsum quid dicere, idq; sibi incognitum fateri, cùm falsi judicium, sicut & veri, necessario oriatur ex præcognitis.
units.tr: So far, then, I have spoken of the first part of astral science, namely astronomy. Now that I have bidden it farewell, I turn my discourse to the other part, which is called divinatory and is the μαντικὴ [mantikē]. Here I am about to stir up against myself a great crowd of scourgers of astrology. So I shall need the club of Hercules and the shield, and a battering ram. Yet my adversaries are not so great that forces must be enlisted to assist me against them. You, hearers, judge according to your own discernment and prudence. If I put forward anything that may perhaps seem too harsh to your ears, I shall soften it; if I have detracted anything from the truth, I shall correct it; but if I speak the truth, do not be angry. Many learned men have attacked this part of the science of the stars in great volumes. There is in people's hands a jumble of accusations, not written by Pico but excerpted from older commentaries, which were gathered long before to censure this divinatory art. These were refuted by Bellantius and certain other learned men. Many light and silly cavils are also raised, whose repetition would be lengthy and whose refutation is unnecessary. And, if it is permitted to speak the truth, Pico of Mirandola, a man otherwise most learned, was the wretched scourge of the astrologers; he publicly assailed and condemned the art, which he did not know and did not understand, piling up arguments from every side. Is this the conduct of a well-bred man, to attack publicly what he has either never known or never understood? O the times! But certain modern writers too, who have assailed this art in published works, have drawn their darts from him, and they are all the more bitter and virulent the more ignorant each of them is of this divine art. For among the diseases of a world now on the point of collapse, this sore rages above all: those who openly profess their own ignorance of the art nonetheless persuade themselves that they can refute things they do not know, because they judge them to be false. Yet it is ridiculous to say something is false while confessing that one does not know it, since a judgment of falsity, like a judgment of truth, necessarily arises from prior knowledge.

units.la: Hac persuasione tumefacti plaustris argumentorum in Astrologiam procedunt, ut quis miretur tantum posse aliquem armorum adversus artem comparare, quæ tamen nihilominus maneat & stet inconcussa, & nehilum[?] quidé[?] labefactata. Nunquam enim illa sibi ab istis timuit, nunquam quicquam remisit à veritate sua, adeò, ut palmæ instar versus onera sua consurgere altius merito eam dixeris. Cogitare potius deberent, non temerè esse ab eruditissimorum & sapientissimorum hominum judiciis recedendum, qui cùm hujus artis utilitatem & usum cognovissent, tanquam vitæ utilem posteris eam tradendam existimarunt. Et arrogantia est cum summa dementia venari choragium aliquod gloriæ ex insectatione & exagitatione artium, quæ sunt gravi autoritate & judicio doctorum & prudentum receptæ, ac rationalis experientiæ exemplis ac testimoniis indubitatæ fidei munitæ. His igitur calumniatoribus, quibus velut canibus ad vomitum reditus semper patet, cùm videam calumnias illorum facilè rescindi posse atq; extirpari, utile ac pernecessarium duxi, pastomide[?] os occludere, multorum animos ab erroribus liberare, divinæq; arti pristinum honorem & & gloriam restituere. Quænám verò & quidnam illa Astrologia? Est ars divinandi judicandiq; ex astrorum motu, positu, & irradiationibus de futuris in sublunari mundo eventibus. Partes illa habet (celebriorum consensu) duas: Universalem & particularem. Effectiones enim siderum ad subjecta relatæ corpora, dupliciter considerantur, quatenus scilicet in amplos aëris terræq; extenduntur tractus, iisq; res sublunares afficiunt, aut solis hominum imprimuntur corporibus. Universalis totas gentes, regiones & urbes, specialis seu particularis singulorum hominum fata demonstrat, quæ dicitur à genituris genethlialogica, cujus exacta cognitio haberi non potest, nisi universalis scientiam quis habuerit, quia universalia majori vi & efficacia à causis suis moventur.
